tools.name: get_profile
tools.title: Get the signed-in Prodigo profile
tools.description:
Return the signed-in Prodigo profile: a stable opaque id, name, e-mail and the
workspace (organisation) this account belongs to. Call this first in a session.
Returns {"id": "...", "name": "...", "email": "...", "nickname": "<workspace>"}.

tools.name: list_capabilities
tools.title: List the connections available to this account
tools.description:
List which connections this account has configured on Prodigo (jira,
confluence, pega_rules, pega_service_mcp, build_mcp) as booleans, plus where to
configure a missing one. Use it to decide which workflow is possible before
starting a job.

annotations.title: List the connections available to this account

tools.name: optimize_user_story
tools.title: Optimize a user story
tools.description:
Optimize a single user story through ARCHY's agent swarm.

Returns the optimized story plus priority score and reasoning.
Pass `rag_session_id` from `ingest_reference_pdf` to ground the swarm in a PDF.
`conversation_id`/`user_id` (injected by the agent) enforce grounding in the
connected Pega project, if any — including a project the user connected in an
earlier conversation.

tools.name: optimize_jira_epic_subtasks
tools.title: Optimize the stories of a Jira epic
tools.description:
Run ARCHY's full Jira batch: fetch sub-tasks, optimize each, write descriptions back,
generate meta-stories for parent stages, and update parents.

Jira credentials prefer the requesting user's stored connection (resolved by
`user_id`, injected by the agent) and fall back to the environment (JIRA_HOST,
JIRA_EMAIL, JIRA_API_TOKEN, PROJECT_KEY). Override the project by passing
`project_key`. `processing_scope` accepts "all" or "newest".

SAFE DEFAULT — optimizes ONLY the LAST sub-task (the user story). This is the
SimplyDash demo (build the full backlog, then optimize the last sub-task) and
a safe default for any optimize: it never runs the whole project, which on a
real backlog (100+ sub-tasks × ~3-4 min each via o3) would run for hours and
blow timeouts. To optimize the ENTIRE backlog you MUST pass `optimize_all=true`
(only when the user explicitly asks to optimize every story). `optimize_limit=N`
optimizes the FIRST N. `demo_mode` is accepted for compatibility but is no
longer required — the last-sub-task default already gives the demo behavior.

annotations.title: Optimize the stories of a Jira epic

tools.name: start_optimize_jira_epic_subtasks
tools.title: Start optimizing a Jira epic's stories
tools.description:
Start the Jira optimize batch as a BACKGROUND job; returns a `task_id` IMMEDIATELY.

PREFER THIS over `optimize_jira_epic_subtasks` (which BLOCKS for the whole batch and,
on a multi-minute run, can drop the chat stream). Each story takes ~2-3 minutes, so
this returns at once and you POLL `get_jira_batch_status(task_id)` until it reports
done — that keeps the chat responsive and drives the live "X/Y stories" progress card.
Same parameters / safe default (last sub-task only unless `optimize_all`/`optimize_limit`).

annotations.title: Start optimizing a Jira epic's stories

tools.name: get_jira_batch_status
tools.title: Get epic optimization status
tools.description:
Check a `start_optimize_jira_epic_subtasks` batch by its `task_id`.

Returns `running` with the live `X/Y stories` count + elapsed seconds while in
progress (poll again shortly), or the final summary once complete.

tools.name: create_and_optimize_user_story
tools.title: Create an optimized story in Jira
tools.description:
Optimize a single user story through ARCHY's swarm AND create it as a new issue
in the project's Jira backlog (synchronous — returns the result in one call).

NOTE: the swarm optimization can take 1-3 minutes. If your MCP client enforces a short
per-tool timeout (Codex defaults to 60s), either raise it (`tool_timeout_sec`) or use
the non-blocking `start_create_and_optimize_user_story` + `get_user_story_status` pair.

Jira credentials are read from the environment (JIRA_HOST, JIRA_EMAIL, JIRA_API_TOKEN,
PROJECT_KEY). Override the target project with `project_key`. The issue type is
auto-discovered for the project (Story / User Story / Task as available) — pass
`issue_type` only to force a specific one. If `summary` is omitted it is derived from
the optimized story. Pass `rag_session_id` from `ingest_reference_pdf` with
`enable_rag_lookup=true` to ground the swarm in a PDF. Pass
`story_format_mode="jira_style"` to mirror a reference story's structure AND tone,
or `story_format_mode="hybrid"` to keep Prodigo's own structure and only adapt
tone/vocabulary (quality checks always apply either way) — normally forced by the
conversation's story format setting, not something you need to pass yourself.

Returns the new issue key, a browse URL, and the optimized content. If creation fails
after a successful optimization, the optimized text is still returned so no work is lost.

annotations.title: Create an optimized story in Jira

tools.name: start_create_and_optimize_user_story
tools.title: Start creating an optimized story in Jira
tools.description:
Start optimizing a single user story AND creating it in the Jira backlog as a
BACKGROUND job, returning immediately with a `task_id` (no waiting).

Use this instead of `create_and_optimize_user_story` when your MCP client has a short
tool timeout, since the swarm optimization can take 1-3 minutes. Then poll
`get_user_story_status(task_id)` until it reports done; it returns the new issue key,
URL, and optimized story. Same parameters as `create_and_optimize_user_story`.

annotations.title: Start creating an optimized story in Jira

tools.name: get_user_story_status
tools.title: Get story creation status
tools.description:
Check a background `start_create_and_optimize_user_story` job by its `task_id`.

Returns 'running' (poll again shortly), the final result (issue key + URL + optimized
story) once done, or an error message if it failed.

tools.name: get_jira_story
tools.title: Read a Jira story
tools.description:
Read a Jira story by its key (e.g. `PPT-5589`) and return it as markdown:
title, description and acceptance criteria. Use this whenever the user names an
issue key — including one YOU created earlier with create_and_optimize_user_story —
instead of asking them to paste the story. `project_key`/`user_id` are injected.

tools.name: generate_pega_technical_design
tools.title: Generate a Pega technical design
tools.description:
Generate a Pega Infinity 24 technical design (markdown) for a user story, GROUNDED
in the Pega project connected to this conversation.

Give EITHER `story` (the full story text) OR `story_key` (a Jira key such as
`PPT-5589` — the story is read from Jira, so NEVER ask the user to paste a story
that already exists in Jira; passing the bare key as `story` also works).

When a Pega project is bound to the conversation (connect_pega_project), the design is
built against that application's REAL rules: existing rules/classes are reused and listed
under "Existing artefacts reused"; "Artefacts to create" holds only genuinely new
artefacts. The first line of the design says whether it was grounded and in which
project. `model` overrides the configured model. `project_key`/`user_id`/
`conversation_id` are injected by the agent.

tools.name: ingest_reference_pdf
tools.title: Index a reference document
tools.description:
Index a local PDF for RAG so subsequent `optimize_user_story` calls can ground answers
in it. Returns a `rag_session_id` to pass back in with `enable_rag_lookup=True`.

tools.name: ingest_pega_project
tools.title: Index a connected Pega application
tools.description:
Ground a freshly-fetched Pega project in RAG for THIS conversation, AND for
this user's future conversations too.

Call this right after the pega-connector's `fetch_project` returns: pass its
`app_id` and `rag_session_id` — BOTH are plain strings from the fetch result.
Do NOT pass a file path: the manifests directory is resolved SERVER-SIDE from
the shared export volume (`PEGA_EXPORT_DIR/manifests/<app_id>`). Indexes the
project's rules into the conversation's RAG session AND records a durable binding
so that EVERY subsequent story this conversation creates is automatically grounded
in this project's real rules + dependency graph — no need for the model to thread
`rag_session_id` or call the `pega_*` tools. This is a ONE-TIME action per user,
like connecting the Pega operator login: once bound here, EVERY future conversation
for this user inherits it automatically too — do not tell the user they need to
reconnect the project in a new chat. `conversation_id`/`user_id` are injected by
the agent. Isolation is per `rag_session_id`.

tools.name: connect_pega_project
tools.title: Connect a Pega application
tools.description:
Connect a Pega PROJECT end-to-end in ONE call: fetch its rules (METERED,
billable — confirm with the user before calling), build the export + dependency
graph, bind the project to this conversation, and index it for grounding.

This replaces the old two-step "fetch_project then ingest_pega_project" flow —
everything after the fetch is automatic; a fetch failure leaves no binding.
`application`/`version` come from `list_pega_applications` (confirm the exact
name + version with the user first). `conversation_id`/`user_id` are injected
by the agent. Returns a summary with rule/edge counts, or an actionable error
(e.g. the Pega instance is unreachable, or the export must be uploaded from
inside the client network).

tools.name: ingest_blueprint
tools.title: Read a Pega Blueprint
tools.description:
Parse a Pega Blueprint into a PREVIEW Epic -> Story -> SubTask tree. NO Jira writes.

Accepts a blueprint as a dict or a JSON string, validates it is a Pega Blueprint
(pyCandidateCaseTypes at root or under pyDADInfo), transforms it via ARCHY's pure
parser, and returns human-readable markdown: the tree (epics -> stories -> sub-tasks
with titles), aggregate stats (case-types/stages/steps/skipped), and any parse
warnings. This tool performs ZERO Jira calls — use `create_backlog_from_blueprint`
to actually create the backlog. `project_key` is accepted for symmetry but unused
here (no writes happen).

tools.name: analyze_blueprint
tools.title: Analyze a Pega Blueprint
tools.description:
Gap-analyse a Pega Blueprint against Pega case-design best practices. NO Jira writes.

Run this BEFORE building the backlog when the user wants a completeness check
("garbage in = garbage out" — a weak blueprint yields weak user stories). Accepts a
blueprint as a dict or JSON string and returns a markdown report: an overall
completeness score, per-case-type strengths/gaps, and prioritised recommendations,
grounded in Pega Academy best practices (single business outcome with a clear
description; a starting AND a resolution stage; alternate/exception stages; steps
detailed with descriptions; a data model with fields; SLAs; decision logic).

The report language MATCHES the blueprint's language (French blueprint -> French
report; otherwise English). This tool performs ZERO Jira calls.

tools.name: get_blueprint_questions
tools.title: Get open questions about a Blueprint
tools.description:
Return ONLY the clarifying questions for a blueprint (for the GUIDED flow).

Unlike analyze_blueprint, this returns NO completeness score, NO structural
recommendations and NO "fix in Pega" CTA — just the questions whose answers make
the user stories complete and unambiguous (undefined roles/approvers, decision
criteria, exception paths, SLAs), in the blueprint's own language. Returns a JSON
block the guided flow uses to ask the user. NO Jira writes.

annotations.title: Get open questions about a Blueprint

tools.name: create_backlog_from_blueprint
tools.title: Create a Jira backlog from a Blueprint
tools.description:
Create the full Epic -> Story -> SubTask backlog from a Pega Blueprint in Jira.

Parses the blueprint, connects to Jira (creds from JIRA_HOST/JIRA_EMAIL/
JIRA_API_TOKEN/PROJECT_KEY env; override the project with `project_key`), and creates
the hierarchy with correct parent linkage (Stories under their Epic, Sub-tasks under
their Story). Returns markdown listing the created issue keys, per-level counts,
browse URLs, and any errors/warnings — the resolved project key is echoed back so you
can confirm the write target (threat T-03-08).

Set `dry_run=True` to PREVIEW counts with ZERO writes. `concurrency` bounds the number
of in-flight creates per level (default 6).

`demo_mode` is accepted for API compatibility but NO LONGER slices the create:
the SimplyDash demo flow builds the FULL structure here and then optimizes the
LAST sub-task in a SEPARATE optimize_jira_epic_subtasks(demo_mode=true) call.
So this tool always creates the entire Epic/Story/SubTask tree.

NOTE: this is a single synchronous call. A typical blueprint (a handful of epics with
their stages/steps) completes well inside an MCP client's tool timeout because the
creates run concurrently per level. For a very large blueprint that might exceed a
short client timeout, parse first with `ingest_blueprint` to gauge size; a durable
start/poll variant can be added later if needed (the existing
start_create_and_optimize_user_story + get_user_story_status pair is the pattern).

annotations.title: Create a Jira backlog from a Blueprint

tools.name: get_reference_stories
tools.title: Get reference stories from Jira
tools.description:
Fetch recent well-formed Jira stories to use as the swarm's `example_user_story`.

Connects to Jira (creds from env; override the project with `project_key`), fetches
recent non-sub-task stories that have a description (newest first), and returns
markdown listing each story plus the single BEST `example_user_story` (a canonical
"As a ..." form when available) clearly labeled so you can pass it straight into
`optimize_user_story` / `optimize_jira_epic_subtasks`. Pass a custom `jql` to override
the default selection (read-only, runs under the authenticated user's permissions).
`limit` caps how many stories are fetched (default 10).

tools.name: verify_story
tools.title: Verify a story against the running application
tools.description:
Verify a Jira story against the running Pega app — END TO END, in ONE call.

This single tool does the WHOLE job server-side: reads the story's acceptance
criteria, drives the Pega app in a headless browser (navigate + snapshot),
judges each criterion against the on-screen evidence (PASS / GAP / FAIL with
analysis, proof and remediation), posts a detailed report to Jira, and saves it
to the verification dashboard. You (the model) do NOT drive the browser yourself
— just call this once and relay the returned summary in the user's language.
Returns a markdown summary (or a clear blocker, e.g. a login wall).

annotations.title: Verify a story against the running application

tools.name: start_verify_backlog
tools.title: Start verifying a backlog
tools.description:
Verify the Jira backlog against the Pega app — BACKGROUND batch.

Returns a task_id IMMEDIATELY; the app polls get_verify_backlog_status and shows
a live "k/N verified" card. It scans the backlog and verifies every story that
HAS acceptance criteria (i.e. has been written/optimized) — skipping raw,
un-optimized sub-tasks fast (no browser drive). Each verified story is checked
server-side (browser + judged criteria + screenshot proof) and saved to the
dashboard. `limit` caps how many stories-with-criteria to verify (default: all).
You (the model) call this ONCE and STOP — do not poll; the app drives progress.

tools.name: get_verify_backlog_status
tools.title: Get backlog verification status
tools.description: Check a start_verify_backlog batch by task_id. Live 'k/N stories' + summary.

tools.name: start_retrodoc
tools.title: Start documenting an existing application
tools.description:
Reverse-document a RUNNING Pega app — BACKGROUND crawl (Retrodoc).

SOURCE (``mode``): "auto" (default) uses the RULES of the Pega project connected to this
conversation (or to the user) PLUS the live screen exploration when a rule export exists
— the rules give the authoritative process, the screens the real UI — and says so in its
reply; without a connected project it documents from the screens only. "screens" forces
screens-only; "combined" asks for rules+screens and falls back to screens (explained).
``language`` ("fr"|"en", defaults to the UI language the app injects) is the language of
the generated document; ``audience`` "business" (default, the DSF) or "technical".

Logs in as EVERY connected operator (one per business role — Settings promises
"connect one operator per business role so the documentation ... see[s] the whole
process, not just one role's screens"), crawls each role's screens SEQUENTIALLY
(safety-gated: never mutating actions; full interactive crawling requires
``uat_attested`` — a non-prod/UAT with stubbed integrations — else it degrades to
passive read-only), describes each unique screen, and synthesizes ONE merged
document + backlog covering every role. Returns a task_id IMMEDIATELY; the app
polls get_retrodoc_status and shows a live "k/N screens" card. Call this ONCE and
STOP — do not poll; the app drives progress.

tools.name: get_retrodoc_status
tools.title: Get documentation status
tools.description: Check a start_retrodoc crawl by task_id. Live 'k/N screens' + summary.

tools.name: get_retrodoc_document
tools.title: Get the generated documentation
tools.description: Return the generated retrodoc document (markdown) for a crawl / conversation.

tools.name: start_build
tools.title: Build a design into a Pega branch
tools.description:
Build a technical design's rules into a Pega BRANCH via the Build MCP (F6).

DEFERRED RULES ARE NOT THE END: after get_build_report lists what needs the user's input
(e.g. a Connect-REST endpoint), call this AGAIN with the SAME `branch` and `rule_inputs` —
a JSON array like provide_rule_inputs' ([{"rule_name","endpoint_url","http_method"?,
"auth_profile"?,"applies_to"?}]). The rules that got inputs are built into that EXISTING
branch (its change request is reused — never a second branch); nothing else is re-created.

`application` is the Pega application to build INTO (alias, label or name, e.g.
`wr-bank`). The user controls this via Settings → Pega application; the agent
injects it (or the alias from `pega_app_url`) so it is NEVER hardcoded. If the
user names a different application, pass it here.

`model` is the conversation's selected model alias (injected by the agent); the
rule-logic generation uses it, so the ONE model the user picks drives the build and
a sovereign pick stays cloud-free. `detail` controls how much logic is authored:
"logic" (default) generates REAL
rule bodies (activity steps, data-transform mappings, decision-table rows, when
conditions, e-mail bodies), grounded in the Pega authoring skills, and falls back
to a shell per rule if generation or authoring fails; "shell" authors minimal
placeholder rules only. Either way the branch is never merged — it is a draft for
human review.

Parses the design's "Artefacts to create" table, authors the buildable rules
(Property / Validate / Service Level — proven first-pass — plus Activity, Data
Transform, When, Decision Table and Correspondence as minimal valid SHELLS the
developer completes in Dev Studio) into a governed branch with create-rule, and
DEFERS structural/UI/integration types (Case Type, Flow, Section, Data Page,
Connect-REST, flow shapes ...) with a reason. If NOTHING is buildable, no branch is
opened at all and the result says so. NEVER MERGES — the branch is the human approval gate. When no live Build MCP
is configured, or dry_run=True, it SIMULATES and still returns a full report. Returns
a task_id IMMEDIATELY — EXCEPT when it answers "Nothing to build" (a grounded design
found every artefact already exists): then there is NO job, NO task_id, nothing to poll
and no report to open — relay that sentence and stop. Otherwise; the app polls get_build_status ("k/N rules") and opens the
build report at the end. Call this ONCE and STOP — do not poll; the app drives it.

annotations.title: Build a design into a Pega branch

tools.name: get_build_status
tools.title: Get build status
tools.description: Check a start_build run by task_id. Live 'k/N rules' + summary.

tools.name: get_build_report
tools.title: Get build report
tools.description: Return the F6 build report (markdown) for a build run / conversation.

tools.name: start_remediation_loop
tools.title: Start the build, judge and fix loop
tools.description:
Close the loop on a built branch (F7): JUDGE it, feed gaps back to the builder, REBUILD.

Runs the independent Judge (a DIFFERENT model, browser evidence) against the branch in a
BRANCH-AWARE context (Pega "Branch development" + Preview App — the only context where
unmerged branch rules render), feeds its GAP/CONTRADICTED findings back to F6 as scoped
fixes, rebuilds into the SAME branch, and re-judges — up to max_iterations (default 2,
hard cap 3), stopping on all-pass / no-improvement / no-derivable-fix / spend cap. NEVER
MERGES. ``app_url`` must be the branch-aware Preview URL for the Judge to see branch rules;
without it the Judge degrades to a rules-only cross-check. Returns a task_id IMMEDIATELY;
poll get_remediation_status, then get_remediation_report. Call ONCE and STOP.

annotations.title: Start the build, judge and fix loop

tools.name: get_remediation_status
tools.title: Get remediation status
tools.description: Check a start_remediation_loop run by task_id.

tools.name: get_remediation_report
tools.title: Get remediation report
tools.description: Return the F7 remediation report (markdown) for a run / conversation.

tools.name: start_migration_plan
tools.title: Plan a migration into Pega
tools.description:
Produce a MIGRATION PLAN from a technical design and PAUSE for approval — authors
NOTHING. Reconciles each proposed rule against the TARGET app's existing ruleset
(create/update/skip/conflict), orders rules into dependency waves, and stores a durable,
reviewable plan. Approve it with approve_plan to start the durable build.

`design` must be the markdown from generate_pega_technical_design. `app_id` is the export
id of the target app to reconcile against (e.g. 'WRBANK!01.01.01'); omit it to skip
reconciliation (everything becomes a create). Env PEGA_WORK_CLASS / BUILD_ORIGIN_RULESET
win over the class/ruleset params (single-app deployments).

tools.name: get_plan_status
tools.title: Get migration plan status
tools.description: Status of a migration plan + its durable execution (poll after approve_plan).

tools.name: approve_plan
tools.title: Approve a migration plan
tools.description: Approve a migration plan and START its durable build (never merges the branch).

tools.name: get_plan_report
tools.title: Get migration plan report
tools.description:
A readable report of a migration plan: per-rule verdict/wave/status PLUS the rules that
need YOUR input to finish (so nothing is ever silently dropped — collaborate to reach 100%).

tools.name: provide_rule_inputs
tools.title: Provide inputs for deferred rules
tools.description:
Supply the inputs a plan's deferred rules needed, then BUILD them into the SAME branch —
the collaboration close-the-loop toward 100% (#133). Call this after get_plan_report lists
rules that 'need your input'; it NEVER opens a new branch and NEVER merges.

`rule_inputs` is a JSON array; each item names one rule and its inputs. For an integration
rule (Connect-REST) the endpoint is all that's required:
  [{"rule_name": "FetchLatestTemplate", "endpoint_url": "https://api.bank/tpl",
    "http_method": "GET", "auth_profile": "BankAuth",
    "applies_to": "MyOrg-App-Data-Template", "response_property": "DataSource.pyResponseData"}]

Only `rule_name` + `endpoint_url` are mandatory for an integration. Rules that need a config
change instead (coverage-gated types, or Dev-Studio enrichment) are reported back, not
force-built. Poll get_plan_report to see the updated per-rule outcome.

tools.name: list_built_branches
tools.title: List branches built by Prodigo
tools.description:
List the Pega branches Prodigo authored into (F6/F7/F8), with their lifecycle status.

Shows what was built into each branch and where it is (built -> judged -> merged /
discarded). Deletion is a Dev Studio action — the Build MCP has no delete tool — so
this is the review/cleanup list, not a delete surface.

tools.name: set_branch_status
tools.title: Record a branch as merged or discarded
tools.description: Advance a recorded branch's lifecycle status: built | judged | merged | discarded.

annotations.title: Record a branch as merged or discarded

tools.name: start_migration
tools.title: Execute an approved migration plan
tools.description:
Accelerate a legacy migration (F8): reverse-doc a SOURCE app, rebuild onto a TARGET.

Retrodocs the SOURCE app READ-ONLY (never writes it), turns each recovered story into a
technical design, BUILDS those rules onto a SEPARATE TARGET branch (F6), and — if a
``target_preview_url`` is given — judges the target against the source in comparison
mode. Produces a source->target traceability record with gaps flagged. NEVER merges;
REFUSES to build onto the source. Returns a task_id IMMEDIATELY; poll
get_migration_status, then get_migration_report. Call ONCE and STOP.

tools.name: get_migration_status
tools.title: Get migration status
tools.description: Check a start_migration run by task_id.

tools.name: get_migration_report
tools.title: Get migration report
tools.description: Return the F8 migration report (markdown) for a run / conversation.

tools.name: create_backlog_from_retrodoc
tools.title: Create a Jira backlog from documentation
tools.description:
Push the retrodoc-generated backlog to Jira (reuses the blueprint write engine).

``dry_run=True`` previews counts without writing. Set ``dry_run=False`` to create
the Epics/Stories/Sub-tasks in the configured Jira project.

annotations.title: Create a Jira backlog from documentation

tools.name: document_pega_from_rules
tools.title: Document an application from its rules
tools.description:
Document an EXISTING Pega app from its RULE EXPORT, enriched by a live screen crawl.

Reads the connector's rule export (case types, ordered stages, flows, user steps,
calculation and decision rules, reports, data) and synthesizes a document + a
ready-to-build backlog, rendered as the retrodoc document. ``app_name`` selects the
export (e.g. 'WRBank').

COMBINED BY DEFAULT for a real Pega app: when a portal URL + stored credentials are
available, a bounded READ-ONLY (passive, navigation-only) crawl of the running portal is
run and its real screens ground the step detail; the rules supply the authoritative
process/logic. Falls back to the rules-only document when the portal is unreachable. Set
``combine_screens=false`` to force rules-only.

``audience`` = "business" produces the **Document de Spécification Fonctionnelle (DSF)**
— a functional spec for business readers, ZERO Pega vocabulary, process/actors-centric,
with a process diagram; "technical" (default) produces the as-built technical spec for
the Pega team. ``language`` = "fr" | "en" (defaults to English). Each (audience,
language, variant) is generated and persisted independently.

annotations.title: Document an application from its rules

tools.name: audit_mcp_readiness
tools.title: Audit a Service MCP for agent readiness
tools.description:
Audit an EXISTING Pega project for safe exposure over an Infinity 26 Service MCP endpoint.

Runs entirely on the connector's rule export (works on ANY Pega version). Classifies
every candidate exposable artifact (case type, flow, flow action, automation, report,
data page, data model) as RECOMMENDED_EXPOSE / EXPOSE_WITH_GUARDRAIL / DO_NOT_EXPOSE /
INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION, each with a written reason grounded in the dependency graph.
A DO_NOT_EXPOSE / guardrail verdict shows the concrete reaching path from the artifact
to the external integration, correspondence or notification rule it can trigger, and
RECOMMENDED artifacts get a draft MCP tool definition with justified behaviour hints.

``app_name`` selects the export (e.g. 'WRBank'); if omitted it is resolved from the
project bound to this conversation. ``audience`` = "business" produces a risk/governance
report with zero Pega vocabulary; "technical" (default) includes the draft tool
definitions. ``language`` = "fr" | "en".

annotations.title: Audit a Service MCP for agent readiness

tools.name: judge_mcp_tools
tools.title: Judge MCP tool descriptions
tools.description:
Measure how reliably an AI agent selects the RIGHT MCP tool from a set of tool
descriptions (feature F2). For each tool it generates realistic task prompts, asks a
SEPARATE model (a different alias from any description writer -- never grading its own
homework) to pick a tool, and reports per-tool selection accuracy as stacked counts
(correct / wrong tool / no tool / ambiguous), with a specific diagnosis (name collision,
vague verb, missing parameter semantics, overlapping scope with a named sibling) for any
tool below the bar. Pass ``tool_manifest`` (a list of {name, description, params}); if
omitted, the tools are taken from the MCP Readiness Audit's draft definitions for the
bound Pega project.

tools.name: optimize_mcp_tool_descriptions
tools.title: Rewrite MCP tool descriptions
tools.description:
Rewrite a set of MCP tool names/descriptions for reliable agent selection, and PROVE the
improvement (feature F2). Enforces a consistent action-oriented naming scheme, a one-sentence
purpose, explicit parameter descriptions with an example, and a stated return shape, then runs
the selection-accuracy harness BEFORE and AFTER so the delta per tool is measurable. Pass
``tool_manifest``; if omitted, the tools come from the MCP Readiness Audit's draft definitions
for the bound Pega project. Returns the before/after report plus the optimised definitions.

tools.name: connect_service_mcp
tools.title: Connect a Pega Service MCP
tools.description:
Register a Pega Service MCP endpoint for this user (F5) — a ONE-TIME action.

Generic: pass ANY project's Infinity 26 Service MCP endpoint URL. Registered ONCE,
it is remembered for this user and reused automatically in EVERY future conversation
(the same way the connected Pega operator/app URL already is) — never register it
again unless the endpoint itself changes. After this, stories are grounded in the
tools the application already exposes, any story-relevant capability that exists as
a rule but is NOT exposed is flagged as a blocker, and start_retrodoc / the MCP
readiness tools automatically use it. Does NOT require connecting/ingesting a Pega
rules project first — this is a separate, independent capability. An unreachable
endpoint is still saved (Pega/network hiccups are transient); it simply grounds
nothing until it becomes reachable.

tools.name: judge_document
tools.title: Judge a document against the live application
tools.description:
Have an INDEPENDENT judge verify the generated documentation against the REAL app.

This is the "check of the check": a SEPARATE agent (a different model, a skeptical prompt)
re-inspects the running application and rules each documentation claim CONFIRMED /
CONTRADICTED / GAP / UNVERIFIABLE, grounded in what it actually observes on screen — NOT
in the facts the document's author used. It never grades its own homework. Screen-checkable
claims are verified against the live app (strong); structural claims are cross-checked
against the rules (weak, same source, flagged as such); unreachable/unobservable claims are
honestly marked UNVERIFIABLE. Returns a short summary; the app renders the full evidence
report (per-claim verdicts + the screenshots the judge looked at). Call this AFTER the
documentation exists, when the user asks to verify / audit / check / "faire vérifier" it.

annotations.title: Judge a document against the live application

tools.name: judge_backlog
tools.title: Judge a backlog against the live application
tools.description:
Independently verify the Jira BACKLOG STORIES against the running app — BACKGROUND.

The "check of the check" for the backlog: an INDEPENDENT judge (a different model, grounded
in the LIVE app) reads each written user story's acceptance criteria and rules them
CONFIRMED/CONTRADICTED/GAP/UNVERIFIABLE against what it observes on screen — it never grades
its own work. Crawls the app ONCE and reuses that evidence for every story (efficient).
Returns a task_id IMMEDIATELY; the app polls get_verify_backlog_status and shows a live
"k/N verified" card, and each result lands on the Verification dashboard + the per-story
backlog badge. `limit` caps stories-with-criteria. ``language`` ("en" | "fr" | "ar",
defaults to the UI language the app injects) is the language the judge writes its
analyses in. Call this ONCE and STOP — do not poll.

annotations.title: Judge a backlog against the live application

tools.name: verification_report
tools.title: Get a verification report
tools.description:
Persist + post a DETAILED story verification report (PASS / FAIL / GAP per criterion).

Each item in `criteria` should be a dict with:
  - id        e.g. "AC1"
  - text      the acceptance criterion
  - status    PASS | FAIL | GAP  (GAP = committed but not implemented)
  - analysis  WHY this verdict — what was checked and what was found on screen
  - remediation  what to do to close a GAP/FAIL (the concrete fix); "" for PASS
  - evidence  the concrete proof: the DOM/snapshot finding (e.g. the element/
              test-id found, or "no element matching X in the snapshot")
Writes a detailed report to Jira as an ADF comment AND persists it (with all
fields + timestamp) to verification_results for the dashboard + pane badges.
Call this ONCE at the end of a verification run.

tools.name: learn_house_style
tools.title: Learn the client's story house style
tools.description:
Learn how THIS client writes user stories, from their own existing stories,
and use that standard for every story from now on.

Sources (combine any): Confluence `page_ids` or a `cql` query (needs a
Confluence connection); Jira `jira_keys` or a `jira_jql` query (needs the Jira
connection); or `pasted` — raw story texts the user gave you directly. Prefer
3-5 stories from DIFFERENT journeys. Reads their format AND reasoning method,
shows what it understood, and stores it so it can be corrected.
`conversation_id`/`user_id` are injected by the agent.

annotations.title: Learn the client's story house style

tools.name: get_house_style
tools.title: Get the learned house style
tools.description:
Show the house style currently learned for this client — the format and the
reasoning method every new story follows. `user_id` is injected by the agent.

tools.name: correct_house_style
tools.title: Correct the learned house style
tools.description:
Correct something in the learned house style — the customer's own words win.

`corrections` maps a field to its corrected value, e.g.
`{"header_table_fields": ["Case", "Role", "User story", "When", "Then", "Priority"]}`
or `{"baseline_rule": "always start from the current screen"}`. A corrected style
is never silently overwritten by a later re-learn. `user_id` is injected by the
agent.

tools.name: forget_house_style
tools.title: Forget the learned house style
tools.description: Delete the learned house style for this client. `user_id` is injected.

tools.name: publish_story_to_confluence
tools.title: Publish a story to Confluence
tools.description:
Publish a story to Confluence as a page in the client's own house-style format
(header table, change bullets, field specification table), optionally linked to a
Jira issue. Confirm with the user before calling — this publishes to their wiki.
`user_id` is injected by the agent.
